title: Level 1 · Design your mission
intro: Every NASA science mission is built from four segments: Launch, Space, Ground and User. First decide what you'll study; then pick one card per segment and bring it into your mission. Careful: budget isn't everything. Falling short puts the mission at risk, and spending on what isn't justified lowers your maturity (CML).
pickMission: Pick a destination to see its requirements and unlock the mission cards.

objective.title: Science requirements
objective.question: What phenomenon or remote destination will we study, and why?

segments.title: Mission segments
segments.question: Drag (or press "Add") one card per segment into "Configured mission". Each cost is deducted from the budget.

launch.question: Which rocket and launch services take us to the target orbit?

space.question: Which spacecraft (CubeSat) will do the science?

ground.question: Which stations and antennas will receive the data?

user.question: How will scientists process and analyze the data?

segReq.user: any approach; higher level = more science, but it costs more.

reqHelp: Science requirements drive the engineering: in each segment pick what the destination needs, no less (it would fail) and not much more (waste).

launch.consider: The real cost of the rocket and its services, the payload it can carry and, above all, whether it has the energy to send the spacecraft to your destination.
launch.avoid: Paying for a much bigger rocket than needed: it doesn't improve the science and takes money from the other segments. Don't pick one that can't reach the destination either.

space.consider: The spacecraft must survive and operate where you're going: available power (sunlight drops with distance), communications, propulsion and instruments.
space.avoid: Buying a deep-space spacecraft for a nearby target (unjustified overfunding) or a near-class one for a distant target (technical failure).

ground.consider: Distance defines how much antenna you need to hear the spacecraft. Farther = bigger antennas and more contact hours.
ground.avoid: Booking the Deep Space Network for the Moon (idle capital) or neglecting this segment: without ground stations, the data never arrives.

user.consider: Data is only worth something if someone processes, calibrates and publishes it. A better approach multiplies the science you get.
user.avoid: Forgetting this segment: a mission without data processing spends its whole budget and delivers no science results.

bank.title: Available options
bank.help: Card bank by segment. Press "?" to see what to consider.

config.title: Configured mission
config.help: Acceptance area: one card per segment. Drop a new one here to replace the previous one.

insufficient.launch: {name} doesn't have the energy to send the spacecraft to {dest}. Without a proper launch, there is no mission.
insufficient.space: {name} isn't built for {dest}: it would lack power, protection or communications. You need at least "{required}". Risk of technical failure.
insufficient.ground: {dest} requires level {req} communications and this network only reaches level {lvl}. The data wouldn't reach Earth. You need at least "{required}".
insufficient.user: This approach falls short of what {dest} demands.

oversized.launch: A smaller rocket is enough for {dest}: you're paying ${extra}M for capability the mission won't use.
oversized.space: {dest} doesn't need "{name}": that's ${extra}M of capability without technical justification.
oversized.ground: {dest} doesn't need "{name}": ${extra}M in antennas the mission won't use.
oversized.user: You're spending ${extra}M more than the data team can use.

flags.overBudget: The mission costs ${spent}M and the cap is ${total}M (${over}M over). No NASA design review approves a mission that exceeds its budget: swap or remove cards.

review.title: Design review
review.start: Bring one card from each segment into "Configured mission". Here you'll see whether the mission passes review.
review.clean: Balanced mission: every segment covers what the destination demands, with no wasted capital.

blockersTitle: To continue you still need to:

blockers.name: Name the project.
blockers.insufficient: Swap the {seg} card: it doesn't meet the destination's requirements.
blockers.overBudget: Cut ${over}M: the mission exceeds its budget.

ready: "{name}" passes the review. Max reachable CML: {cml}.
